pr_body:
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/7864
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/4267 (partial)

 This PR builds upon the side resizing PR. For text elements, when resized from "left" and "right" (or "w" and "e"), we support text wrapping and unwrapping. 

# follow-ups/TBD

- [ ] drag-with-text-tool during creation to set the initial text width
- [ ] paste of long text should limit the width (disable `autoResize`)
- [x] TBD: on font size change, keep width constant (upon further review it makes more sense from the viewpoint of user intention)

issue_context.title: Text area tool
issue_context.body:
It would be nice to have a text area tool, that is, draw a rectangle within which text auto-wraps.

It could perhaps replace the current text tool:
1. Double-click to start typing. This creates an auto-sizing text box (current functionality)
2. Deselect. This locks box size.
3. Further editing that box will attempt to wrap.

Click and dragging instead of double-click would create a fixed box size with wrapping from the get-go.

An indicator at the bottom right would show that text is overflowing the boundaries. Double-clicking on it would auto-size the height of the box, keeping the width the same.

The only sticky point is dragging the size handles. That currently scales the text as a graphic; in this mode, it should rescale the area the text is allowed to flow into.
comments: We support binding text to shapes now https://twitter.com/aakansha1216/status/1471509326674030592

Text area (bounding box) is something which is separate from container-bound text, and we want to support this. The only thing to figure out is how it should behave.

- Figma allows you to draw a rectangle bounding box, but the height is not constrained at all (it overflows the bounding box).

	![figma-text-bounding-box](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/146422327-70f92928-b84f-4da5-8e37-0e4f035cd431.gif)
- Miro allows you draw a "linear" single-line bounding box, and the box autogrows as you type (basically the same behavior as we have right now with container-bound text).

	![miro-text-bounding-box](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/146422565-3f4960c9-1c9f-4564-b40e-f98298ba4906.gif)


Figma and Miro approaches above are effectively identical except in UX.

That said, Miro does allow this hybrid resizing approach:

- resizing from east/west reflows text as per new width
- resizing from corners retains aspect ratio but adapts text size <--- we wanted to do this for container-bound shapes if you hold shift. It should work like this for non-container bound text, but probably not if not holding shift.

Will this allow us to drag the rectangle tool also to adjust the width?

Currently I have to drag the corner, but this changes the height and I only want to extend the width without adjusting the height. (Same can be said of changing vertical dimensions).

Not that my personal preference matters, but I like how miro handles the text flow. Also like how they handle the resizing for all shapes becuase they give you handles that make it easy to grab both edges and corners of every object.

review_comments: can this go into else of line 327 ? since you are checking if its `e` || `w`

Without the `if` check here, scale from line 266 would not be zero and it'll trigger logic unrelated to `e` and `w`. I didn't really want to touch the logic that was working well for corner resizes. So the `if` check is here for that purpose.
